notes.meaning: These verses name the four main clans that came from the sons of Issachar. Issachar is counted right after Judah because this tribe camped under Judah's standard. The names match the family list from Genesis, though the spelling of a couple of names changed slightly over time.

The men of fighting age in Issachar numbered 64,300. This was an increase of nearly ten thousand men since the first census at Mount Sinai. God blessed this tribe with steady growth during the wilderness years.

Zebulun was divided into three main clans named after the sons of Zebulun who originally went down to Egypt. Their military registration came to 60,500 men. This was a gain of over three thousand soldiers since the first count forty years earlier.

Joseph was given two tribes instead of one because Jacob adopted his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim. Manasseh is named first here because his tribe had grown much larger during the wilderness journey. Both tribes together fulfilled the special promise of blessing given to Joseph.

Manasseh's descendants are traced through his son Machir and his grandson Gilead. These two men founded large clans that later received an inheritance on the east side of the Jordan River. Machir's line became the main branch for the entire tribe.

Gilead had six sons who each became the head of a major clan in Manasseh. These six family lines formed the main divisions of the tribe. Listing them here prepared Israel to divide the land fairly among these families when they entered Canaan.

Zelophehad stood out because he had five daughters but no sons. In Israel, land was normally passed down through sons, so this family faced losing its name and property. Their unusual situation led to an important case that brought new laws of inheritance from God.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars observe that while this case granted daughters the right to inherit land, the reform was later limited by requiring them to marry within their own tribe to prevent property from transferring outside the clan.

notes.meaning: Manasseh counted 52,700 men of fighting age. This was an increase of 20,500 men, which was the largest gain of any tribe in the entire census. This dramatic growth fulfilled Jacob's ancient prophecy that Joseph would be a fruitful vine.

Ephraim's tribe was divided into three clans from his sons, along with a fourth clan from his grandson Eran. These four groups made up the official military branches of the tribe. They carried on the legacy of Joseph's younger son.

The total number of fighting men in Ephraim was 32,500. The tribe had dropped by eight thousand men since the first census at Mount Sinai. Even though Ephraim was currently smaller than Manasseh, God's promise that Ephraim would become a great power remained in effect.

Five clans of Benjamin came directly from his sons. Earlier records in Genesis listed ten sons for Benjamin, but some of those brothers likely died without having children. The families that survived grew into these five strong clans.

Benjamin's oldest son Bela had two sons named Ard and Naaman. Because these two families grew so large, they were counted as full clans alongside the clans of Benjamin's own sons. This brought the total number of recognized clans in Benjamin to seven.
The fighting men of Benjamin numbered 45,600. This was an increase of 10,200 men since the first census was taken. God rebuilt and multiplied the tribe during their years in the desert.

Dan had only one recorded son, Shuham, so the entire tribe grew from a single family line. In spite of starting with just one son, Dan counted 64,400 men, making it the second-largest tribe in all of Israel. This showed clearly that the growth of a family depends entirely on God's blessing rather than human advantages.
